title: Checking Taxa Presence in Samples
text: One key challenges environmental sequencing studies determining whether detected taxa likely actually present sampling sites. vignette demonstrates use taxinfo’s occurrence checking functions validate likelihood taxa presence based known geographic distributions. taxinfo’s utilities, functions can accept either phyloseq object cleaned taxonomic names vector taxonomic names (taxnames parameter). algorithm used assign taxonomic names must stringent enough avoid false positives. Moreover, recommend using gna_verifier_pq() clean taxonomic names disambiguating synonyms correcting misspellings.

title: Checking Taxa Presence in Samples
text: main functions checking taxa presence : tax_occur_check(): Core occurrence checking function individual taxa tax_occur_check_pq(): Check occurrence likelihood within radius around samples tax_occur_multi_check_pq(): Check multiple locations simultaneously

title: Checking Taxa Presence in Samples
text: Use occurrence data filter taxa unlikely present:
code: # Set threshold for likely presence (e.g., at least 5 occurrences within 100km) min_occurrences <- 5  likely_present <- occurrence_check |>   filter(count_in_radius >= min_occurrences) |>   pull(taxa_name)  # Filter phyloseq object to keep only likely present taxa # Note that all samples are kept, use clean_pq if you want to remove empty samples data_filtered <- select_taxa_pq(data_clean, taxnames = likely_present) #> Warning in verify_pq(physeq, verbose = verbose): At least one of your sample #> contains less than 500 sequences. #> Warning in verify_pq(physeq, verbose = verbose): At least one of your taxa is #> represent by less than 1 sequences. #> Warning in verify_pq(physeq, verbose = verbose): At least one of your samples #> metadata columns contains NA. #> Number of non-matching ASV 0 #> Number of matching ASV 20 #> Number of filtered-out ASV 14 #> Number of kept ASV 6 #> Number of kept samples 137  compar <- MiscMetabar::track_wkflow(   list(     "initial" = data_clean,     "filtered" = clean_pq(data_filtered)   ),   verbose = FALSE ) #> Cleaning suppress 0 taxa and 110 samples. #> Compute the number of clusters #> Compute the number of samples knitr::kable(compar)

title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: Beyond occurrence data, taxinfo integrates multiple knowledge sources enrich taxonomic data Species salience public knowledge (Wikipedia), species interactions (GLOBI), scientific literature (OpenAlex), custom database content. vignette demonstrates leverage functions create comprehensive taxonomic @tax_table.

title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: tax_get_wk_info_pq(): Wikipedia data page statistics tax_globi_pq(): Species interaction data GLOBI tax_oa_pq(): Scientific literature OpenAlex tax_info_pq(): Custom database integration (TAXREF, traits, etc.) tax_photos_pq(): Taxonomic images media Note: functions can work either phyloseq objects vectors taxonomic names (taxnames parameter). using phyloseq object, results automatically added tax_table. using taxnames, tibble returned.

title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: Wikipedia rich source public interest knowledge species. integrating Wikipedia data, can proxy societal attention given different taxa. number page views, mean page length number languages species covered can provide insights cultural significance measuring sort species salience public knowledge.

"))), na.rm = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE),     n_host_pathog = mean(map_dbl(pathogenOf, ~ stringr::str_count(.x, ";")), na.rm = TRUE),     n_host_parasit = mean(map_dbl(parasiteOf, ~ stringr::str_count(.x, ";")), na.rm = TRUE),     Guild = Guild[1]   ) |>   mutate(n_host_parasit = ifelse(is.na(n_host_parasit), 0, n_host_parasit)) |>   mutate(n_host_pathog = ifelse(is.na(n_host_pathog), 0, n_host_pathog)) |>   filter(nb_inter > 0) |>   ggplot(aes(     y = forcats::fct_reorder(taxa_name, nb_inter),     x = nb_inter,     color = Guild,     size = log10(1 + Abundance)   )) +   geom_point() +   geom_text(aes(label = paste(n_host_pathog, "-", n_host_parasit)),     size = 2.5, color = "black", nudge_y = 0.2   ) +   theme_idest() +   labs(     title = "Interactions in GLOBI",     subtitle = "First and second number indicate the number of verified taxonomic\nentity whose the taxa are respectively pathogen or parasite.",     x = "Number of interactions",     y = "Taxa",     color = "Guild following FunGuild",     size = "Number of sequences (log10)"   )

mutate(across(     all_of(c("hasHost", "parasiteOf")),     ~ stringr::str_detect(.x, stringr::fixed(target_taxon_name))   )) |>   mutate(interaction_type = case_when(         parasiteOf ~ "parasiteOf",     hasHost ~ "hasHost",     .default = "other"   ))  # Visualize interaction networks ggplot(interaction_summary, aes(   x = interaction_type, y = nb,   fill = interaction_type )) +   geom_violin() +   geom_jitter(col = "grey40", alpha = 0.2, height = 0) +   labs(     title = "Species Interaction Diversity",     x = "Interaction Type",     y = "Number of Target Taxa"   ) +   theme_idest() +   theme(legend.position = "none") ggplot(   interaction_summary,   aes(x = taxa_name, y = target_taxon_name) ) +   geom_segment(     aes(       x = taxa_name, xend = target_taxon_name,       y = 0, yend = 1,       color = interaction_type,       linewidth = nb     ),     alpha = 0.6   ) +   geom_point(aes(x = taxa_name, y = 0), size = 3, color = "darkred") +   geom_point(aes(x = target_taxon_name, y = 1), size = 3, color = "darkgreen") +   scale_linewidth_continuous(range = c(0.5, 3), name = "Number of interactions") +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Interaction type") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     axis.title = element_blank(),     axis.text.y = element_blank(),     axis.ticks = element_blank(),     panel.grid = element_blank(),     legend.position = "bottom"   ) +   coord_flip() +   labs(title = "Fungal-Plant Interaction Network") library(ggraph)  edges <- interaction_summary |>   select(     from = taxa_name, to = target_taxon_name,     weight = nb, type = interaction_type   )  nodes <- data.frame(   name = unique(c(edges$from, edges$to)) ) |>   mutate(     node_type = ifelse(name %in% unique(edges$from), "Fungal", "Plant")   )  graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE, vertices = nodes)  ggraph(graph, layout = "fr") +   geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight, color = type), alpha = 0.6) +   geom_node_point(aes(fill = node_type), size = 5, shape = 21, color = "black") +   geom_node_text(aes(label = ifelse(node_type == "Fungal", name, "")), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +   scale_edge_width_continuous(range = c(0.5, 3), name = "Number of interactions") +   scale_edge_color_manual(values = c("grey60", "purple", "cyan", "green")) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("Plant" = "lightgreen", "Fungal" = "orange")) +   theme_idest(grid = FALSE, axis_text_size = 0) +   labs(     title = "Fungal-Plant Interaction Network",     y = "",     x = ""   ) #> Warning: ggrepel: 1 unlabeled data points (too many overlaps). title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: French taxonomic data, integrate TAXREF:
code: # Load TAXREF data (example file) taxref_file <- system.file("extdata", "TAXREFv18_fungi.csv",   package = "taxinfo" )  # Add TAXREF information data_clean_taxref <- tax_info_pq(data_clean,   file_name = taxref_file,   csv_taxonomic_rank = "LB_NOM",   csv_cols_select = NULL,   col_prefix = "taxref_" ) psm <- psmelt(data_clean_taxref) |>   group_by(currentCanonicalSimple) |>   mutate(across(everything(), ~ replace(., . == "" | . == "NA", NA))) |>   filter(!is.na(currentCanonicalSimple)) |>   summarise(     taxref_FR = unique(taxref_FR),     taxref_HABITAT = unique(taxref_HABITAT),     occurence = sum(Abundance > 0, na.rm = TRUE),     Abundance = sum(Abundance, na.rm = T),     Order = unique(taxref_ORDRE),     taxref_NOM_VERN = unique(taxref_NOM_VERN)   ) |>   filter(!is.na(Order))  ggplot(psm, aes(   x = forcats::fct_reorder(currentCanonicalSimple, occurence),   y = 1 + occurence,   fill = Order )) +   geom_col() +   geom_text(aes(label = currentCanonicalSimple,                 fontface = ifelse(is.na(taxref_FR), "italic", "bold.italic")),     y = -1, hjust = 1, size = 2.5   ) +   geom_text(aes(label = taxref_NOM_VERN, y = 2 + occurence), size = 3, color = "black", hjust = 0) +   coord_flip() +   scale_fill_viridis_d() +   labs(     title = "Frequences of Taxa with French common names",     subtitle = "Bold taxa are already known in France (TAXREF).",     x = "Taxa",     y = "Number of occurences (samples)"   ) +   theme_idest() +   theme(     axis.text.y = element_blank(),     axis.ticks.y = element_blank()   ) +   scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.05))) #> Warning: Removed 13 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_text()`).

title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: Assess information completeness across sources:
code: # Calculate information completeness completeness_analysis <- data_fungi_full@tax_table |>   as.data.frame() |>   summarise(     gbif = 100 * mean(!is.na(Global_occurences)),     wikipedia = 100 * mean(!is.na(lang)),     globi = 100 * mean(!is.na(nb)),     taxref = 100 * mean(!is.na(taxref_CD_NOM)),     openalex = 100 * mean(!is.na(n_doi))   ) |>   tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "data_source", values_to = "completeness") # Visualize data completeness ggplot(completeness_analysis, aes(   x = reorder(data_source, completeness),   y = completeness, fill = data_source )) +   geom_col() +   geom_hline(yintercept = 100) +   coord_flip() +   geom_label(aes(label = paste0(round(completeness, 1), "%"), y = completeness / 2), hjust = 0.5, col = "black", fill = rgb(1, 1, 1, 0.5)) +   scale_fill_viridis_d() +   labs(     title = "Data Source Completeness",     x = "Data Source",     y = "Percentage of Taxa with Data"   ) +   theme_idest() +   ylim(c(0, 100)) +   theme(legend.position = "none")

title: Adding External Information: Wikipedia, GLOBI, and Custom Databases
text: Identify taxa limited information:
code: # Identify knowledge gaps knowledge_gaps <- data_fungi_full@tax_table |>   as.data.frame() |>   select(Global_occurences, lang, nb, taxref_CD_NOM, n_doi, currentCanonicalSimple) |>   mutate(     gbif_info = !is.na(Global_occurences),     wk_info = !is.na(lang),     oa_info = !is.na(n_doi),     taxref_info = (!is.na(taxref_CD_NOM) | taxref_CD_NOM == "NA"),     globi_info = (!is.na(nb))   ) |>   mutate(taxref_info = ifelse(is.na(taxref_info), FALSE, taxref_info)) |>   mutate(     info_score = gbif_info + wk_info + oa_info + taxref_info + globi_info   ) |>   arrange(info_score)  # Number of available sources of information per taxa (ASV here) knowledge_gaps |>   pull(info_score) |>   table() #>  #>  0  1  3  4  5  #>  9  8  1 16 11   # Number of available sources of information per taxonomic names (current canonical simple) knowledge_gaps |>   distinct(currentCanonicalSimple, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   pull(info_score) |>   table() #>  #>  0  1  3  4  5  #>  1  6  1 11  7  # Poorly knowns taxonomic names (current canonical simple) knowledge_gaps |>   distinct(currentCanonicalSimple, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   filter(info_score <= 2) |>   pull(currentCanonicalSimple) #> [1] NA                "Xylodon"         "Antrodiella"     "Helicogloea"     #> [5] "Phanerochaete"   "Auricularia"     "Marchandiomyces" knowledge_gaps |>   distinct(currentCanonicalSimple, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   filter(!is.na(currentCanonicalSimple)) |>   ComplexUpset::upset(     intersect = c("gbif_info", "wk_info", "oa_info", "taxref_info", "globi_info"),     keep_empty_groups = TRUE,     wrap=TRUE,set_sizes = F          ) +    labs(     title = "Knowledge Gaps Across Data Sources",     subtitle = "Number of taxa names with available data from each source and their intersections"   ) + theme_idest()

title: GBIF-based Functions for Occurrence Data
text: Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) world’s largest repository biodiversity occurrence data. taxinfo package provides seamless integration GBIF specialized functions retrieve occurrence data, create distribution maps, analyze biogeographic patterns taxa phyloseq objects.

title: GBIF-based Functions for Occurrence Data
text: tax_gbif_occur_pq(): Retrieve occurrence counts GBIF plot_tax_gbif_pq(): Create distribution maps range_bioreg_pq(): Analyze biogeographic ranges tax_check_ecoregion(): Validate occurrences ecoregions tax_occur_check_pq(): Check occurrences within geographic radius Note: Functions like tax_gbif_occur_pq() tax_occur_check_pq() can work either phyloseq objects vectors taxonomic names (taxnames parameter). using phyloseq object, results automatically added tax_table. using taxnames, tibble returned.

title: Getting Started with taxinfo: Augment phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: taxinfo package provides comprehensive tools augmenting phyloseq objects taxonomic-based information various external data sources. vignette provides big picture overview package’s capabilities workflow. large part ASV OTUs, hereafter referred taxa, obtained metabarcoding studies often identified species level. taxa genus species level identification can still enriched valuable information various databases. taxinfo package allows easily integrate information phyloseq objects. Taxinfo also create body evidence presence species samples testing likelihood taxon present.

title: Getting Started with taxinfo: Augment phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: taxinfo integrates multiple authoritative data sources enrich taxonomic data: 🔍 Data Verification: Verify standardize taxonomic names using Global Names Architecture 🌍 Biodiversity Data: Access GBIF occurrence data species interactions GLOBI 📚 Knowledge Integration: Retrieve Wikipedia data scientific literature OpenAlex 🗺️ Geographic Analysis: Analyze biogeographic ranges create distribution maps 🔬 Advanced Tools: Sequence-based verification multi-source occurrence validation

title: taxinfo - Augment Phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: taxinfo package provides comprehensive tools augmenting phyloseq objects taxonomic-based information various external data sources. seamlessly integrates data GBIF, Wikipedia, GLOBI, OpenAlex, TAXREF, databases enrich taxonomic analyses.

title: taxinfo - Augment Phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: taxinfo designed work phyloseq objects provides functions : Verify clean taxonomic names using Global Names Architecture (GNA) Retrieve occurrence data GBIF biodiversity databases Access taxonomic traits various databases including FungalTraits Get Wikipedia information including page views, links, content statistics Fetch scientific literature data OpenAlex Access interaction data GLOBI (Global Biotic Interactions) Validate geographic occurrences ecoregions biogeographic regions Retrieve taxonomic photos media information

text: functions can work either: - Phyloseq objects: Automatically enriches tax_table (default behavior) - Taxonomic name vectors: Returns tibbles standalone queries

title: taxinfo - Augment Phyloseq Objects with Taxonomic Information
text: Following Darwin core standards, key terms used taxinfo (camel case naming convention): - scientificName: full scientific name authorship date information known (e.g., “Stereum ostrea (Blume & T.Nees) Fr., 1838”) - genus: Just genus part (e.g., “Stereum”) - specificEpithet: Just species epithet part (e.g., “ostrea”) - namePublishedInYear: year name published (e.g., “1838”) terms come verifier globalnames (camel case naming convention): - currentCanonicalSimple: simplified scientific name without authorship (e.g., “Stereum ostrea”). correspond concatenation genus specificEpithet fields.

what: Create Species-Bound Clusters using SWARM algorithm — cluster_sbc
title: Create Species-Bound Clusters using SWARM algorithm — cluster_sbc
text: function creates Species-Bound Clusters (SBC) phyloseq object containing taxa (ASV/OTU) sequences taxonomy based proposition Riley *et al.* 2025 (<https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-025-02284-x>). SBC (Species bound cluster) defined "clusters include   ESVs assigned one species, sequence similarity threshold can vary   clusters" (Riley *et al.* 2025   <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-025-02284-x>). uses SWARM algorithm cluster taxa within taxnames (e.g. Genus species) based sequence similarity, allowing variable d values optimize clustering. Run swarm d=1 d=max_d, taxnames (e.g. Species binomial name),  find lowest d clusters taxa assigned taxnames one  cluster. taxnames represented one taxa, clustered.  Taxnames containig "NA" considered unassigned. default, unassigned  ASVs clustered cluster without counting taxnames.  Set include_unassigned = FALSE force cluster included taxa  given taxnames none unassigned ones. maximum d reached, keep clustering d print warning.  strict_sbc = TRUE, taxa corresponding strict SBC clustered  return phyloseq object, cases, taxa whose taxnames  clustered multiple clusters whose cluster contains multiple taxnames  NA cluster_ID removed phyloseq object. function returns data.frame cluster assignments  optimal d value taxnames, well modified phyloseq object  cluster information added taxonomy table.

what: Verify taxonomic assignment using BLAST against NCBI nucleotide database — tax_retroblast_pq
title: Verify taxonomic assignment using BLAST against NCBI nucleotide database — tax_retroblast_pq
text: idea take binomial taxonomic name assigned ASV/OTU Genus_species level, search sequences NCBI nucleotide database corresponding taxon name (additional filters including marker name), retrieve sequences fasta format, perform BLAST search retrieved sequences ASV/OTU sequences. can therefore test ASV/OTU best BLAST hit corresponds taxon name one assigned ASV/OTU. Moreover, can also detect cases better taxonomic assignment can proposed based BLAST results limited species name already present phyloseq object. Note function need physeq object works list taxonomic names (taxnames parameter function).

title: Verify taxonomic assignment using BLAST against NCBI nucleotide database — tax_retroblast_pq
code: tax_retroblast_pq(   physeq,   taxonomic_rank = "currentCanonicalSimple",   marker = NULL,   id_cut = 99,   retmax = 500,   add_to_phyloseq = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE,   start_date = NULL,   end_date = NULL,   min_length = 300,   max_length = 4000,   refseq_only = FALSE,   sup_params = "NOT uncultured[Title] NOT clone[Title]",   ... )

title: Verify taxonomic assignment using BLAST against NCBI nucleotide database — tax_retroblast_pq
text: physeq (required) phyloseq object taxonomic_rank (required, default = "currentCanonicalSimple") column(s) present @tax_table slot phyloseq object. Can vector two columns (e.g. c("Genus", "Species")). marker (required) character vector marker names used search term. example, c("", "internal transcribed spacer") fungal sequences. Note marker names present title sequences NCBI nucleotide database. id_cut (default: 99) minimum  good match. 100 value means perfect matches considered good matches. retmax (default: 500) maximum number sequences retrieve NCBI nucleotide database taxon name. add_to_phyloseq (logical, default TRUE) TRUE, new phyloseq object returned new columns tax_table. verbose (logical, default TRUE) TRUE, prompt messages. start_date start date search. NULL (default), search limited date. date must format "YYYY-MM-DD". end_date () end date search. NULL (default), search limited date. start_date NULL end_date NULL, end_date set today's date. date must format "YYYY-MM-DD". min_length (int) Minimum sequence length consider search. max_length (int) Maximum sequence length consider search. refseq_only (logical, default FALSE) TRUE, sequences RefSeq database retrieved. RefSeq curated non-redundant database sequences NCBI. FALSE, sequences NCBI nucleotide database retrieved. Note using refseq_only = TRUE experimental may lead sequence retrieved taxon names. sup_params (char) Additional parameters added search term. default set ("uncultured[Title] clone[Title]") exclude uncultured clone sequences. ... Additional parameters passed [MiscMetabar::blast_to_phyloseq()] including: `nproc`, `e_value_cut`  `args_blastn`

title: Verify taxonomic assignment using BLAST against NCBI nucleotide database — tax_retroblast_pq
text: Either list (add_to_phyloseq = FALSE) new phyloseq object, add_to_phyloseq = TRUE, new columns based  `tib_retroblast` tibble describe : list composed two elements:   1. `tib_retroblast`: tibble one row taxa phyloseq object:      - `blast_queried`: (logical) queried names sequences      - `blast_result`: (logical) Number queried names least one       blast result      - `good_assign`: (logical) Number good assignation (best blast      hit       one assigned ASV/OTU)      - `alt_assign`: Number alternative assignation proposed      (best blast hit        phyloseq object)      - `taxa_name`: Taxonomic name used query NCBI nucleotide database 2. `entrez_search`: list rentrez::entrez_search results   taxon name

text: physeq (optional) phyloseq object. Either `physeq` `taxnames` must provided, . taxnames (optional) character vector taxonomic names. taxonomic_rank (Character, default "currentCanonicalSimple") column(s) present @tax_table slot phyloseq object. Can vector two columns (e.g. c("Genus", "Species")). verbose (logical, default TRUE) TRUE, prompt messages. time_to_sleep (numeric, default 0.5) Time sleep two queries mycoDB, seconds. add_to_phyloseq (logical, default NULL) TRUE, add spore size information phyloseq object. title: Extract spore size from mycoDB — tax_spores_size_pq
text: `add_to_phyloseq` TRUE, returns phyloseq object new columns tax_table slot: `spore_size`, `spore_length`, `spore_width`. `add_to_phyloseq` FALSE, returns data.frame columns `taxa_name`, `spore_size`, `spore_length`, `spore_width`.

title: Extract spore size from mycoDB — tax_spores_size_pq
text: Adrien Taudiere

title: Extract spore size from mycoDB — tax_spores_size_pq
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ data_fungi_mini_cleanNames <- data_fungi_mini |>   gna_verifier_pq() data_fungi_mini_spore_size <- tax_spores_size_pq(data_fungi_mini_cleanNames)  psmelt(data_fungi_mini_spore_size) |>   group_by(taxa_name) |>   summarise(     spore_length = as.numeric(unique(spore_length_mean)),     spore_width = as.numeric(unique(spore_width_mean)),     Abundance = sum(Abundance),     Occurence = sum(Abundance > 0, na.rm = TRUE)   ) |>   ggplot(aes(x = spore_length, y = spore_width, size = Abundance, col = Occurence)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +   ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = taxa_name),     vjust = -0.5,     size = 3,     fontface = "italic",     min.segment.length = 0.2,     force = 4   ) +   labs(     title = "Spore sizes extracted from mycoDB",     x = "Spore length (\u00b5m)",     y = "Spore width (\u00b5m)",     col = "Number of samples",     size = "Number of sequences"   ) +   theme_idest()  # Example with ellipses psmelt(data_fungi_mini_spore_size) |>   filter(!is.na(taxa_name) & !taxa_name == "") |>   filter(!is.na(Time)) |>   filter(Abundance > 0) |>   mutate(taxa_name = as.factor(taxa_name)) |>   group_by(taxa_name, Time) |>   summarise(     spore_length = 0.2 * as.numeric(unique(spore_length_mean)),     spore_width = as.numeric(unique(spore_width_mean)),     Abundance = sum(Abundance),     Occurence = sum(Abundance > 0, na.rm = TRUE),     Order = unique(Order)   ) |>   arrange(desc(Abundance)) |>   mutate(     taxa_name_num = as.numeric(taxa_name)   ) |>   filter(!is.na(spore_length)) |>   ggplot(aes(     x0 = log(Abundance), y0 = taxa_name_num / 5,     a = spore_length / 2, b = spore_length / 2 / 5, fill = Order   )) +   coord_fixed() +   ggforce::geom_ellipse(aes(angle = 0), alpha = 0.3) +   ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(     x = log(Abundance), y = taxa_name_num / 5,     label = taxa_name, color = Order   ), size = 2) +   theme_idest() +   theme(axis.text.y = element_blank()) +   labs(x = "Number of sequences (log scale)", y = "Taxa") +   facet_wrap(~Time, ncol = 2)   # Test for difference in mean spore length between sample's factor psmelt(data_fungi_mini_spore_size) |>   filter(!is.na(taxa_name) & !taxa_name == "") |>   filter(!is.na(spore_length_mean)) |>   filter(!is.na(Time)) |>   filter(Abundance > 0) |>   mutate(taxa_name = as.factor(taxa_name)) |>   group_by(taxa_name, Time) |>   summarise(     spore_length = unique(as.numeric(spore_length_mean)),     spore_width = unique(as.numeric(spore_width_mean)),     Order = unique(Order)   ) |>   ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats(Time, spore_length) } # }

title: taxinfo 0.1.2 (Development version)
text: Changed default behavior: add_to_phyloseq parameter now defaults TRUE phyloseq object provided, FALSE using taxnames parameter. makes workflow intuitive - working phyloseq objects, enriched object returned default.

title: taxinfo 0.1.2 (Development version)
text: main functions (gna_verifier_pq(), tax_gbif_occur_pq(), tax_get_wk_info_pq(), tax_globi_pq(), tax_info_pq(), tax_iucn_code_pq(), tax_oa_pq(), tax_occur_check_pq(), tax_photos_pq()) now support taxnames parameter, allowing users query information specific taxonomic names without phyloseq object. Added comprehensive tests taxnames parameter usage across functions. Add functions extract_spores_mycodb() tax_spores_size_pq() retrieve spore size information MycoDB. Add params year_col authorship_col gna_verifier_pq() output year publication authorship information taxa. Add function intra_taxnames_dist() compute pairwise DNA distances among taxa taxonomic names. Add function cluster_sbc() (post)cluster taxa SBC (Species bound cluster) defined “clusters include ESVs assigned one species, sequence similarity threshold can vary clusters” Riley et al. 2025 (https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-025-02284-x). Also add new vignette illustrate use cluster_sbc().

title: taxinfo 0.1.2 (Development version)
text: Updated documentation functions clarify new default behavior add_to_phyloseq. Added examples showing phyloseq taxnames usage patterns. Updated vignettes demonstrate dual-input capability (phyloseq objects vs. taxonomic name vectors). Updated README highlight flexible input options.
